title: Erdős Problem #30 — Maximum size of Sidon sets in $[1,n]$
literal_statement:
Sidon also asked: Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_k \leq n$ and assume that $a_i + a_j$ are all distinct. Put $h(n) = \max k$. Determine or estimate $h(n)$ as accurately as possible. Perhaps
$$h(n) = n^{1/2} + O(1),$$
but this is perhaps too optimistic. I give 500 dollars for a proof or disproof of the conjecture
$$h(n) = n^{1/2} + o(n^{\varepsilon})$$
for any $\varepsilon > 0$.
reason: The all-epsilon error term for maximum Sidon size is much stronger than a construction on selected n; no uniform sharp error mechanism. Literal pair indexing needs source convention, not an ordered-pair wording counterexample.

title: Erdős Problem #33 — Minimal counting function of complements to the squares
literal_statement: Let $b_1 < b_2 < \ldots$ be an infinite sequence of integers, so that every integer is of the form $b + k^2$. Denote by $B(x)$ the number $b$-s not exceeding $x$. [...] I can not determine the smallest possible value of $\limsup \frac{B(x)}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}$. Clearly $B(x) \geqslant x^{\frac{1}{2}}$ holds, but I can not prove that $\liminf \frac{B(x)}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}} > 1$.
reason: Infinite complement with every integer represented requires global density control, not a finite covering certificate. Ellipsis and square-domain conventions require primary clarification before proof.

title: sunflower conjecture
literal_statement:
For a set $U$, a collection $W$ of subsets of
$U$ is called a *sunflower* (or $\Delta$-system) if there is a set
$S \subseteq U$ such that $A \cap B = S$ for all distinct $A, B \in W$; the
number of sets in $W$ is its number of petals.

For positive integers $k$ and $r$, let
$f(k,r)$ denote the smallest nonnegative integer $n$ with the following
property: every family $W$ of sets, each of cardinality at most $k$, with more
than $n$ members contains a subfamily of $r$ sets that is a sunflower. (Such an
$n$ exists, and $f(k,r) \le k!\,(r-1)^k$.)

For every integer $r > 2$ there exists a constant $C = C(r) > 0$, depending only
on $r$, such that

$$
f(k,r) \le C^{k} \qquad \text{for all } k \ge 1.
$$
reason: For each r>2 one exponential base must work for every k; factorial bound printed in statement does not provide this. No full-scope shortcut.

title: Dirac–Motzkin conjecture
literal_statement:
For a finite set $S$ of points in the Euclidean plane, call a line $\ell$ an
*ordinary line* of $S$ if $\ell$ contains exactly two points of
$S$. For an integer $n\geq 3$, let

$$
t_2(n)=\min\bigl\{\,\#\{\ell:\ \ell\ \text{is an ordinary line of }S\}\ :\ S\subset\mathbb{R}^2,\ |S|=n,\ S\ \text{not collinear}\,\bigr\},
$$

the minimum being taken over all $n$-element sets of points that do not all lie
on a single line. Then

$$
t_2(n)\ \geq\ \left\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor \qquad\text{for every integer } n\geq 3;
$$

that is, every set of
$n$ points in the plane, not all collinear, determines at least $\lfloor
n/2\rfloor$ lines that pass through exactly two of the points.
reason: All n≥3 is stronger than sufficiently-large-n ordinary-line results; no source check of small exceptions here. Do not count a recollected known theorem as a new proof.

title: Moser's worm problem
literal_statement:
Call a set
$C\subset\mathbb{R}^{2}$ a *cover* if for every rectifiable plane curve $\gamma$
of length $1$ there is a rigid motion $g$ of the plane (a composition of a
rotation and a translation) such that $g(\gamma)\subseteq C$; equivalently,
every such curve has a congruent copy contained in $C$.

Determine

$$
\alpha=\inf\{\operatorname{area}(C)\;:\;C\subset\mathbb{R}^{2}\ \text{is a cover}\},
$$

and exhibit a cover $C$ with $\operatorname{area}(C)=\alpha$, where
$\operatorname{area}$ denotes Lebesgue measure in the plane.

Determine also the corresponding quantity for the convex variant,

$$
\alpha_{\mathrm{conv}}=\min\{\operatorname{area}(K)\;:\;K\subset\mathbb{R}^{2}\ \text{is a convex cover}\},
$$

together with a convex cover attaining this minimum.
reason: Must determine the infimum and attain it for arbitrary rectifiable curves, plus convex variant; a better cover alone is restricted progress.

title: total coloring conjecture
literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with vertex set $V(G)$, edge set
$E(G)$, and maximum degree $\Delta(G)$. A total coloring of
$G$ is an assignment of colors to the elements of $V(G)\cup E(G)$ such that

- no two adjacent vertices receive the same color, - no two edges sharing an
endpoint receive the same color, and - no edge receives the same color as either
of its endpoints.

The total chromatic number
$\chi''(G)$ is the least number of colors in a total coloring of $G$.
Equivalently,
$\chi''(G)$ is the ordinary chromatic number of the total graph $T(G)$, whose
vertices are the elements of $V(G)\cup E(G)$ and in which two such elements are
adjacent exactly when they are adjacent or incident in $G$.

Then for every such graph $G$,

$$
\chi''(G)\leq \Delta(G)+2.
$$
reason: Every finite simple graph with Δ+2 colors; bounded-degree or special-family constructions do not close full scope.

title: Albertson conjecture
literal_statement:
For a finite simple graph $G$, let $\operatorname{cr}(G)$ denote its crossing
number, i.e. the minimum number of pairwise crossings of edges over all drawings
of
$G$ in the plane in which edges are curves meeting only at finitely many points, no three edges cross at a common point, and no two adjacent edges cross; and let $\chi(G)$
denote its chromatic number, the least number of colours in a proper vertex
colouring of $G$. Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices.

For every integer $n \ge 1$ and every finite simple graph $G$ with $\chi(G) \ge
n$,

$$
\operatorname{cr}(G) \ \ge \ \operatorname{cr}(K_n).
$$
reason: Every n and every graph with χ≥n; a few chromatic thresholds do not prove crossing-number comparison uniformly.

title: Vizing's conjecture
literal_statement:
All graphs considered are finite, simple, and undirected. For a graph
$G$ and a vertex $v \in V(G)$, let $N[v] = \{v\} \cup \{u \in V(G) : uv \in
E(G)\}$ denote the closed neighbourhood of $v$. A set $D \subseteq V(G)$ is a
dominating set of $G$ if $\bigcup_{v \in D} N[v] =
V(G)$, and the domination number $\gamma(G)$ is the minimum cardinality of a
dominating set of $G$.

For graphs $G$ and $H$, the Cartesian product $G \,\square\, H$ is the graph
with vertex set $V(G) \times V(H)$ in which two distinct vertices
$(g,h)$ and $(g',h')$ are adjacent if and only if either $g = g'$ and
$hh' \in E(H)$, or $h = h'$ and $gg' \in E(G)$.

For all graphs $G$ and $H$,

$$
\gamma(G \,\square\, H) \;\geq\; \gamma(G)\,\gamma(H).
$$
reason: Every pair of finite graphs in the Cartesian-product domination inequality; special products give no full-scope route.

title: uniqueness conjecture for Markov numbers
literal_statement:
Call a triple $(x,y,z)$ of positive integers a Markov triple if

$$
x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=3xyz,
$$

and call it normalized if $x\le y\le z$. A Markov number is a positive integer
occurring as a coordinate of some Markov triple.

For every Markov number
$c$ there is exactly one normalized Markov triple whose largest element is $c$;
that is, if $(x_{1},y_{1},c)$ and $(x_{2},y_{2},c)$ are normalized Markov
triples, then $x_{1}=x_{2}$ and $y_{1}=y_{2}$.
reason: Uniqueness for every largest Markov number, not generation of triples or finite search. No uniform uniqueness bridge.

title: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture
literal_statement:
For a real number $x\ge 2$ let
$\operatorname{li} x=\int_{2}^{x}\frac{dt}{\log t}$, let
$\varphi$ denote Euler's totient function, and for a positive integer $q$ and an
integer $h$ with $(h,q)=1$ let

$$
\pi(x;q,h)=\#\{p\le x:\ p\ \text{prime},\ p\equiv h \pmod q\}.
$$

For every real $A>0$ there exists a constant $C(A)>0$ such that for all $x\ge 2$
and all real $X$ with $1\le X<x(\log x)^{-A-1}$,

$$
\sum_{q\le X}\varphi(q)\max_{(h,q)=1}\left(\pi(x;q,h)-\frac{\operatorname{li} x}{\varphi(q)}\right)^{2}\le C(A)\,\frac{x^{2}}{\log^{A}x},
$$

the maximum being taken over all residue classes $h$ modulo $q$ with
$(h,q)=1$, and the constant $C(A)$ depending only on
$A$ and in particular being independent of $x$ and $X$.
reason: The literal weighted squared error has constants depending only on A over every admissible x,X; not interchangeable with familiar formulations without proof.

title: Skewes's number
literal_statement: In number theory, Skewes's number is the smallest natural number $x$ for which the prime-counting function $\pi (x)$ exceeds the logarithmic integral function $\operatorname {li} (x).$ It is named for the South African mathematician Stanley Skewes who first computed an upper bound on its value. The exact value of Skewes's number is still not known, but it is known that there is a crossing between $\pi (x)<\operatorname {li} (x)$ and $\pi (x)>\operatorname {li} (x)$ near $e^{727.95133}\approx 1.3972\times 10^{316}.$ It is not known whether this is the smallest crossing. The name is sometimes also applied to either of the large number bounds which Skewes found.
reason: Requires first crossing, not the stated known crossing or another upper bound; a small exact certificate is unavailable.

title: Erdős distinct distances problem
literal_statement:
For a finite set $P\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ let

$$
D(P)=\{\,\|p-q\|_2 \;:\; p,q\in P,\ p\neq q\,\}
$$

be its set of distinct Euclidean distances, and for an integer $n\geq 2$ put

$$
g(n)=\min\{\,|D(P)| \;:\; P\subset\mathbb{R}^2,\ |P|=n\,\},
$$

the minimum being over all sets of $n$ distinct points in the plane.

Then for every real $c$ with $c<1$ there exists a constant $\gamma_c>0$ such
that

$$
g(n)\geq \gamma_c\, n^{c}\qquad\text{for all } n\geq 2;
$$

that is, $g(n)=\Omega(n^{c})$ for every $c<1$.
reason: Every c<1 power lower bound is a known-result lead via stronger distinct-distance bounds. Primary successor body not checked, so no verified resolved status or credit asserted.

title: The $d$-step Conjecture for polytope diameters
literal_statement:
Let $H(n,d)$ denote the maximum graph diameter of a $d$-dimensional polytope with $n$ facets.

**The $d$-step Conjecture.** For every $d \geq 2$,

$$
H(2d,d) \leq d.
$$

The source states that this conjecture is equivalent to the Hirsch Conjecture by the Klee–Walkup theorem. Since the Hirsch conjecture is refuted, this conjecture is also refuted.
reason: Record itself explicitly says equivalent Hirsch conjecture is refuted. No discovery from reproducing d-step refutation; primary proof not audited.

title: Behsaz–Hatami–Mahmoodian's minimum vertex-cover conjecture for generalized Petersen graphs
literal_statement:
Let $P(n,k)$ be the generalized Petersen graph, and let $\beta(P(n,k))$ denote the size of a minimum vertex cover. **Behsaz–Hatami–Mahmoodian's conjecture.** For all $n$ and $k$,

$$
\beta(P(n,k))\leq n+\left\lceil\frac{n}{5}\right\rceil.
$$

Since the paper gives no resolution of this conjecture, its status remains open.
reason: Primary Section5 Theorem4 proof and Corollary3 already give n>3k and parity/small-k cases. Remaining parameters not settled by those constructions; no small counterexample pursued. Prior search gives only a restricted n+2 characterization lead, not full bound.

title: The existence conjecture for p-extremal elementary graphs
literal_statement: Let $p\geq1$ be an integer. A $p$-extremal elementary graph is an elementary graph with $p$ perfect matchings and maximum possible excess $c_p$. **p-extremal elementary-graph existence conjecture.** For every $p\geq1$, there exists a $p$-extremal elementary graph. The source says that all known values of $p$ admit such graphs, but does not establish the assertion in general.
reason: Maximum excess is taken across graphs, while elementary subclass must attain it for each p; definitional existence alone does not prove this. Need primary definitions before treating as tautology.

title: Exact critical threshold for simple games
literal_statement:
Let $c_\mathcal{S}(n)$ denote the maximum critical threshold value among simple games on $n$ voters. **Simple-game threshold conjecture.** For every $n\ge 4$, 

$$
c_\mathcal{S}(n)=\frac{\left\lfloor\frac{n^2}{4}\right\rfloor}{n}.
$$

The paper proves the displayed quantity as a lower bound, improving the previously known bound for odd $n$, but does not establish the matching upper bound.
reason: Exact maximum for every n≥4 needs universal upper bound over simple games. Printed lower bound alone gives no matching argument.

title: Smallest weak Carmichael numbers with a fixed number of prime factors
literal_statement: For a composite integer, call the number of distinct prime divisors its number of prime factors. **Smallest weak Carmichael number conjecture.** For every integer $k\ge 3$, the smallest weak Carmichael number with $k$ distinct prime factors is a Carmichael number. This is stated as a computationally motivated conjecture.
reason: Primary Conjecture2.48 and Remark2.49 checked: k=3 smallest561 and k=4 smallest41041 already source examples; arbitrary k needs global minimality and existence. No new finite instance or theorem.

title: Galvin's minimum-degree conjecture for independent sets
literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree, and let $i(G)$ denote its number of independent sets. Assume that $n\geq 2d$ and $\delta(G)\geq d$. **Galvin's conjecture.**

$$
i(G)\leq i(K_{d,n-d}).
$$

Galvin proved the conjecture for fixed $d$ and sufficiently large $n$, and for all $n$ when $d=1$; the general case remains open.
reason: n≥2d and minimum degree≥d, all d,n. Statement acknowledges known fixed-d large-n and d=1; no promotion of those regimes. General theorem successor needs primary check.

title: Hähnle's connected layer multicomplex diameter conjecture
literal_statement:
Let $H_{\operatorname{c.l.m.}}(n,d)$ be the maximum length of a connected layer multicomplex of rank $d$ on $n$ elements. **Hähnle's conjecture.** For all $n$ and $d$,

$$
H_{\operatorname{c.l.m.}}(n,d)\leq d(n-1).
$$

This is a multicomplex generalization proposed in the Polymath 3 project. The source does not report a resolution of the conjecture.
reason: All ranks and ground-set sizes, bound d(n−1) for connected layer multicomplex length. Requires source convention on length and connectedness; no complete combinatorial argument.

title: Cycle goodness conjecture
literal_statement: For a connected graph $H$, define its **goodness** to be the largest integer $p$ for which $H$ is $p$-good, where $H$ is $p$-good if $R(H,K_p)=(|H|-1)(p-1)+1$. **Cycle goodness conjecture.** For all $n\geq4$, the goodness of the cycle $C_n$ is $n$.
reason: Exact largest p-good parameter for every cycle length n≥4; proving goodness for a few p or n does not determine this maximum uniformly.

title: Prime-power Olson degree conjecture
literal_statement: An integer $d$ is an **Olson degree** if every torsion subgroup of a CM elliptic curve defined over a number field of degree $d$ is determined by the curve's CM data as in the paper. **Prime-power Olson degree conjecture.** $p^n$ is an Olson degree for every prime $p>5$ and all $n\in\mathbb{Z}^+$. The conjecture strengthens the stated prime-power theorem and is supported computationally: no counterexample with $p>5$ was found for $p^n\leq 10^{14}$ unconditionally, or for $p^n\leq 10^{30}$ using computations conditional on the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis. It remains open in general.
reason: Every prime p>5 and every positive power exponent; computational ranges, including conditional GRH range, do not prove Olson property. CM-data definition needs primary.

title: Associativity conjecture for finite Moufang p-loops with p not equal to 3
literal_statement:
Let $L$ be a finite Moufang $p$-loop, where $p\ne 3$. Suppose $L$ is generated by a set $\{a_i\mid i\in I\}$ satisfying

$$
(a_i,a_j,a_k)=1
$$

for all $i,j,k\in I$, where $(x,y,z)$ denotes the associator defined by $(xy)z=(x(yz))(x,y,z)$. **Associativity conjecture.** Then $L$ is associative. The conjecture excludes the prime $3$, which is essential in the paper's constructed counterexample of order $3^{19}$; the stated result is presented as a conjectural affirmative answer to the preceding problem for finite Moufang $p$-loops with $p\ne 3$.
reason: Associating every generator triple must force global associativity in every finite Moufang p-loop for p≠3. Source's p=3 counterexample is excluded; cannot recycle it.

title: Degree 3 dilation conjecture for the infinite square lattice
literal_statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be the infinite square lattice, and let $\delta_0(\Lambda,3)$ denote its minimum stretch factor among degree-$3$ spanners. **Degree 3 dilation conjecture.**

$$
\delta_0(\Lambda,3) =(3+2\sqrt2) \, 5^{-1/2} = 2.6065\ldots
$$

The paper has established the matching upper bound and conjectures that it is optimal; whether the upper bound can be improved is therefore left open.
reason: Exact infimum stretch over every degree3 infinite-lattice spanner needs matching universal lower bound. Existing upper construction cannot supply it.

title: Bezdek–Zamfirescu's X-ray conjecture
literal_statement:
Let $X(\mathbf{K})$ be the smallest number of lines such that every boundary point of a convex body $\mathbf{K}$ is X-rayed along at least one of them. **X-ray conjecture.** For every convex body $\mathbf{K}\subset\mathbb{E}^d$,

$$
X(\mathbf{K})\leq 3\cdot 2^{d-2}.
$$

The conjecture is proved in the plane but remains open in higher dimensions.
reason: Universal dimension convex-body X-ray bound, not planar case. Potential d=1 wording endpoint is a scope correction, not substantive discovery.

title: Akiyama–Watanabe conjecture on induced forests in bipartite planar graphs
literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a simple bipartite planar graph. Write $|G|=|V(G)|$, and let $a(G)$ denote the maximum number of vertices in an induced forest of $G$. **Akiyama–Watanabe conjecture.**

$$
a(G) \geq \frac{5|G|}{8}.
$$

The conjecture was proposed in 1987. The paper proves the weaker lower bound $a(G)\geq \lceil(4|G|+3)/7\rceil$, so the stated $5|G|/8$ bound is not resolved by the supplied text.
reason: Every simple bipartite planar graph needs induced forest of size≥5n/8; weaker ceiling((4n+3)/7) stated bound does not imply it uniformly.

title: Zamfirescu's three-longest-path conjecture
literal_statement: Let a **longest path** of a connected graph be a path of maximum length. **Zamfirescu's conjecture.** For every connected graph, any $3$ of its longest paths have a common vertex. This is an open case of Gallai's question about common vertices of longest paths; the paper gives upper bounds on the distance among longest paths but does not resolve the common-vertex assertion.
reason: Any three longest paths in every connected graph must share a vertex, stronger than pairwise intersection. No Helly bridge established.

title: Common-vertex conjecture for three to six longest paths
literal_statement: Let a **longest path** of a connected graph be a path of maximum length. **Common-vertex conjecture.** For every connected graph, any $k$ of its longest paths have a common vertex for $3\leq k\leq 6$. The cases $k=3,4,5,6$ are presented as open extensions of the three-longest-path question; the paper proves distance bounds but does not establish this common-vertex statement.
reason: Every k in3..6, including prior row's three-path case. Stronger conjunction; do not count overlapping k=3 twice or replace common intersection with pairwise.

title: The degree-associated edge-reconstruction conjecture for trees
literal_statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, and let $dern(T)$ denote the minimum number of degree-associated edge-cards needed to determine $T$ up to isomorphism. **Degree-associated edge-reconstruction conjecture.** For every tree $T$,

$$
dern(T)\leq 2.
$$

The paper supports this with results for caterpillars, star-like trees, and several other tree families, but the assertion for all trees remains open.
reason: Every tree must be determined by two degree-associated edge-cards; small-tree/card conventions and reconstruction universe require primary before trivial endpoint objection.

title: The $F(n)$ upper-bound conjecture for 2-increasing sequences
literal_statement:
Let $F(n)$ denote the maximum length of a 2-increasing sequence of triples from $[n]^3$.

**The $F(n)$ upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
F(n)\le n^{3/2}
$$

for all $n$.

A proof would rule out any improvement over the exponent $3/2$ suggested by the product argument, matching the known lower-bound scale and the computational evidence described in the paper.
reason: Every n and maximum length of arbitrary 2-increasing triples, not an exponent asymptotic with a constant. Product examples do not prove exact upper bound.

title: Trudinger–Wang affine Bernstein conjecture
literal_statement:
Let $u\colon\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be smooth and locally uniformly convex. Write

$$
U=(U^{ij})=(\det D^2u)(D^2u)^{-1},
$$

and

$$
w=[\det D^2u]^{-\frac{n+1}{n+2}}.
$$

Assume that $u$ satisfies

$$
\sum_{i,j=1}^{n}U^{ij}w_{ij}=0.
$$

**Trudinger–Wang's conjecture.** If $n\leq 9$, then $u$ is an elliptic quadratic polynomial. If $n\geq 10$, then there exists a smooth, locally uniformly convex solution of the equation which is not an elliptic quadratic polynomial. The conjecture describes the sharp dimension threshold for the affine Bernstein problem: the low-dimensional assertion is known in the stated setting, while the higher-dimensional existence assertion is supported by the singular counterexample discussed in the source; the combined formulation is treated here as unresolved.
reason: Combined smooth locally uniformly convex global PDE rigidity for n≤9 and nonquadratic existence for n≥10. Singular examples do not meet smooth hypothesis; record's status gloss is not proof.

title: Alternating odd-position conjecture for block decompositions
literal_statement:
Let $B=(0;\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n)$ be any non-trivial block decomposition of even weight $N$. **Alternate odd positions conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{Alt}_{\{\ell_i\mid i\text{ odd}\}}I_{\mathrm{bl}}^{\mathfrak m}(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n)=0.
$$

The conjecture extends the analogous alternating identity for 123-multiple zeta values to arbitrary block lengths. It is proposed after the special case suggested by Borwein, Bradley and Broadhurst; no proof or disproof is given in the source.
reason: Every nontrivial even-weight block decomposition and motivic alternating identity, not numerical zeta identities or a special123 case. Missing algebraic definitions prevent cheap proof.

title: Noel–Scott–Sudakov–Balogh–Wagner centeredness conjecture for product posets
literal_statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer, and let $n_0$ be an integer. Equip the product poset $\{0,1,\ldots,k\}^n$ with the coordinatewise order. A family is centered when its elements are chosen as close as possible to the middle rank, and the poset has the **centeredness property** if, for every family size $M$, some centered family of size $M$ minimizes the number of comparable pairs. **Noel–Scott–Sudakov–Balogh–Wagner conjecture.** For every $k$ there exists an $n_0$ such that if $n\geq n_0$ then the poset $\{0,1,\ldots,k\}^n$ has the centeredness property. This extends Kleitman's theorem for the Boolean lattice, while a counterexample is known for $n=2$ and $k=16$; the asserted eventual centeredness for each fixed $k$ remains open.
reason: For each fixed k an eventual n0 works for every family size M; n=2,k=16 counterexample printed in statement does not refute eventual assertion.

title: Equality of Bernoulli double sums for multiplicative inverses
literal_statement:
Let $z$ and $N$ be integers with $\gcd(z,N)=1$. Let $B_1$ and $B_2$ denote the first and second Bernoulli polynomials, respectively, and interpret $z(k-\ell)\bmod N$ as the residue modulo $N$. Write $z^{-1}$ for the multiplicative inverse of $z$ modulo $N$. **Equality conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{k,\ell=1}^{N-1} B_1(k/N) \, B_2((z(k-\ell)\bmod N)/N) \, B_1(\ell/N)
=
\sum_{k,\ell=1}^{N-1} B_1(k/N) \, B_2((z^{-1}(k-\ell)\bmod N)/N) \, B_1(\ell/N).
$$

The equality was verified numerically for all $N\leq 4001$ and all $z\in\{1,\ldots,N-1\}$ coprime to $N$, and it is also proved for Fibonacci lattice rules in the cited context. A general proof or counterexample is not provided here.
reason: Primary Conjecture1, numerical examples, Lemma5 proof and Conclusion read. Complete cyclic-autocorrelation proof retained in ordinary-337039.md;180 exact unit checks. Routine finite-sum symmetry; live bounded search not novelty clearance. Zero credit.
primary_sections_read: Conjecture1, Lemma5 proof, Corollary1, Section6 Conclusion
complete_proof_coverage_scope: independent ordinary derivation only; not the full source paper

title: Narayanan's sublinear-growth conjecture for the extremal function
literal_statement:
Let $\psi(m)$ denote the minimum possible size of $\mathcal{F}_{\Delta}$ over all $m$-colourings of $\mathbb{N}^{(2)}$.

**Narayanan's conjecture.**

$$
\psi(m)=o(m)\qquad\text{as }m\to\infty.
$$

The source notes that this is known on a subset of the integers of density $1$, but remains unknown for all $m$ as $m$ tends to infinity.
reason: Sublinear psi(m) for all m→∞, not on density1 subsequence already reported. Need exact definition of F_Delta and uniform construction.

title: Infinitely many cyclic groups with the weak acyclic matching property
literal_statement:
For a positive integer $n$, consider the cyclic additive group $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. It has the **weak acyclic matching property** if every pair of finite subsets $A$ and $B$ with $\#A=\#B$ and $A\cap(A+B)=\emptyset$ admits at least one acyclic matching from $A$ to $B$.

**Weak acyclic matching infinitude conjecture.** There are infinitely many $n$ for which $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ has the weak acyclic matching property.

Computations reported in the paper show that the property holds for every $n$ with $1<n<23$. The infinitude claim concerns the broader, weaker matching property and is not resolved there.
reason: Infinitely many cyclic orders with weak acyclic matching for every admissible A,B; finite n<23 checks are already source evidence, not infinitude.

title: Flandrin–Fouquet–Li conjecture on Hamilton cycles in $S_{3,3}$-free bipartite graphs
literal_statement: Let $G$ be a connected balanced $S_{3,3}$-free bipartite graph, where $S_{3,3}$ denotes the corresponding forbidden subgraph. **Flandrin–Fouquet–Li conjecture.** There exists a constant $d$ such that if the minimum degree of $G$ is at least $d$, then $G$ contains a Hamilton cycle. This conjecture was proposed in 1994. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
reason: One fixed minimum-degree threshold must force Hamiltonicity in every connected balanced forbidden-subgraph graph. Induced versus ordinary forbidden S33 must be read; no wording counterexample.

title: Anti-labeling conjecture for hypercubes
literal_statement:
For each integer $n\geq 2$, let $Q_n$ denote the $n$-dimensional cube, with $2^n$ vertices. **Hypercube anti-labeling conjecture.** One has

$$
mc^{nh}_{2^n}(Q_n)=2^{n-2}.
$$

The bound is stated after being shown to be sharp for $n=2,3$. The conjecture asks whether the same exact value holds for every higher-dimensional hypercube.
reason: Primary Theorem18 inductive lower-bound proof, Theorem19 Q3 upper proof and Conjecture20 read. Need universal upper bound for every n≥2; sharp n2,3 instances already published. No computation undertaken.

title: Caterpillar conjecture for block graphs maximizing mean CIS order
literal_statement: Let $n\geq 5$, and let $G$ be a block graph of order $n$. Suppose that $G$ has maximum mean CIS order among all block graphs of order $n$. **Block-graph caterpillar conjecture.** Then $G$ is a caterpillar. This strengthens Jamison's Caterpillar Conjecture from trees to block graphs. The claim has been verified for $5\leq n\leq 11$, but the general case remains open.
reason: Every maximizing block graph of every order n≥5 must be a caterpillar; finding one caterpillar maximizer would not prove all maximizers. Small-order checks already source.

title: Schur-positive trees with a degree-floor vertex
literal_statement: For each integer $n\geq 2$, consider $n$-vertex trees and vertices whose degree is measured in the usual graph-theoretic sense. **The degree-floor tree conjecture.** For every $n\geq 2$, there exists an $n$-vertex tree having a vertex of degree $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ whose chromatic symmetric function is a nonnegative linear combination of Schur functions; equivalently, the tree is Schur-positive. The conjecture would show that the degree bound in the paper’s non-Schur-positivity theorem cannot be improved. It has been checked for all trees with up to $19$ vertices, but remains open in general.

title: Infinite sign-change conjecture for the orthorecursive coefficients
literal_statement:
Let $(c_n)_{n\geq0}$ be the real coefficient sequence, and say that it **changes sign** at $N>0$ when $c_Nc_{N+1}<0$.

**Sign-change conjecture.** The sequence $(c_n)_{n\geq0}$ changes sign infinitely often.

Numerical experiments find sign changes at $0,1,27,533,10457,\ldots$, but do not establish infinitude; the conjecture concerns the continuation of this observed oscillation.

title: Yoshihara's conjecture on complements of irreducible plane curves
literal_statement:
Let $\mathrm{k}$ be an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, and let $C,D\subset {\mathbb P}^2$ be irreducible curves. Two such curves are **projectively equivalent** if an automorphism of ${\mathbb P}^2$ sends $C$ to $D$. Suppose that

$$
\varphi\colon {\mathbb P}^2\setminus C\longrightarrow {\mathbb P}^2\setminus D
$$

is an isomorphism between their complements.

**Yoshihara's conjecture.** Then $C$ and $D$ are projectively equivalent.

The conjecture asserts that the complement of an irreducible plane curve determines the curve up to projective equivalence. It is refuted: a counterexample was given by Blanc in 2009.

title: Sudakov–Verstraëte chromatic-number conjecture for consecutive cycle lengths
literal_statement: For $k\geq 2$, let $\chi_k$ be the largest chromatic number of a graph that does not contain $k$ cycles of consecutive lengths. **Sudakov–Verstraëte's conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 2$, $\chi_k=k+1$. The lower bound $\chi_k\geq k+1$ follows from the complete graph $K_{k+1}$; the paper gives no resolution status for the asserted equality in the supplied text.

title: Sali's conjecture on the extremal size of Armstrong codes
literal_statement:
Let $f(q,3)$ denote the maximum length $n$ for which a $(q,3,n)$-Armstrong code exists. **Sali's conjecture.** For all $q\geq 2$, 

$$
f(q,3)=3q-2.
$$

The construction from orthogonal double covers gives the lower bound $f(q,3)\geq 3q-2$, and the conjecture asserts that this bound is always tight. It is false.

title: The Lorentzian conjecture for normalized Schur P-functions
literal_statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition whose nonzero parts are distinct, and let $P_\lambda$ be its Schur $P$-function. **Schur-$P$ conjecture.** The normalized function

$$
\mathrm{N}(P_\lambda)
$$

is Lorentzian for every such partition $\lambda$. The source reports computational evidence for bounded largest part and number of parts; the assertion remains open.

title: Uniform discreteness of cocompact torsion-free arithmetic lattices
literal_statement: Let $G$ be a connected center-free semisimple Lie group without compact factors. Is the family of all cocompact torsion-free arithmetic lattices in $G$ uniformly discrete; that is, does there exist an identity neighborhood $U\subset G$ such that $U$ intersects trivially every conjugate of every lattice in the family?
reason: One identity neighborhood per G must avoid every conjugate of every cocompact torsion-free arithmetic lattice. Individual-lattice discreteness is not uniform family discreteness.

title: The Douglas–Kazakov third-order phase transition
literal_statement:
For every $T>0$, the limit
$$
F(T)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N^2}\log p_T(I_N)
$$
exists. The function $F$ is smooth on $\mathbb{R}_+^*\setminus\{\pi^2\}$, belongs to $C^2(\mathbb{R}_+^*)$, and its third derivative $F'''$ has a jump discontinuity at $T=\pi^2$, where $p_T(I_N)$ is the value at the identity matrix of the heat kernel at time $T$ on $U(N)$.
